Subject: High p95/p99 TTFT spikes affecting checkout personalization

Hi Hannah / Redwood team,

We're seeing a large, sustained jump in first-token latency (TTFT) for calls to the hosted API that power our checkout personalization. Baseline p95 for TTFT was ~1.1s; starting ~08:45 UTC it jumped to ~3.6s — p99s are spiking to 5-6s. Error rate remains low but throughput is degraded due to head-of-line delays.

Quick facts from our side (samples across 08:40-09:05 UTC):
- endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (us-west host)
- p95 TTFT: 3.6s (previously 1.1s)
- p99 TTFT: 5.2s
- no signature errors, TLS handshakes occasionally time out (observed TCP retransmits and full TLS renegotiation)

We attached a short trace (spark-trace-20261103.json.gz) and a small tcpdump (handshake-pcap-20261103.pcap). Our infra team suspects the issue is an upstream change at the CDN/edge — several TLS sessions are failing to resume and appear to be doing full handshakes repeatedly.

This is high-impact for our checkout flow. Can you triage and share an estimated time to mitigate (ETM)? We may need a short call with your eng/ops.

Thanks,
Marco (on behalf of BrightRetail Ops)

Quick triage notes (short-term findings):
- Observed: increased TLS full-handshake rate on connections originating from our us-west edge pool to BrightRetail's CDN IPs starting ~08:30 UTC. TCP RTTs are within normal bounds; the extra latency comes from repeated full TLS handshakes (session resumption failures).
- Cause hypothesis: BrightRetail's CDN rolled an upstream TLS offload config that changed session-cache settings + aggressive idle timeouts. That makes connection reuse fail and forces full handshakes for requests that used to reuse sessions.
- Impact: TTFT p95 jump because each new request is paying a full handshake. P99 amplified for long-tail where handshakes hit retransmits.

Short-term mitigations we can flip now (low-risk):
1) Increase keepalive and reuse windows on our edge (config rollout to us-west cluster) — reduces odds of full handshake.
2) Temporarily route BrightRetail traffic through our alternate edge-pop in us-east (we have capacity for their production QPS) — new route should avoid the misconfigured CDN path.
3) Enable TLS session tickets on the connection pool for that customer only (force session resumption where possible).

I'll open a targeted rollout for the keepalive change and prepare a traffic shift plan. ETA for keepalive flip: ~20-30m. ETA for routing change (if needed): 45-75m.

Attachments: spark-trace-20261103.json.gz (customer trace), handshake-pcap-20261103.pcap (PCAP excerpt).

— Dev Patel

- Status: mitigation applied; observed TTFT returned close to baseline for most traffic after routing flip. We're tracking a small tail of retries; follow-up with CDN vendor pending.
